name: Hole in the Mountain County Park
note: Lincoln County park on the west edge of Lake Benton, ~800 acres of woodland/prairie. 33 sites all with electric + water (RVs to ~33 ft), dump station, showers, hiking trails. Reservable, open mid-May through October. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Lincoln County Parks: overnight camping with electricity $30 a night, without $25. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Pomme de Terre Campground
note: City of Morris campground on Pomme de Terre Lake, with water and electric sites, tent sites, restrooms and showers, a spray park, a disc golf course, a dock, canoeing, fishing and a playground.  The city shuts the park's water off in mid-October; camping continues without it. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Read on Campspot: one night for 2 adults, site rate before tax, every RV site type a 23-ft rig fits (30 Amp Back-In Site, 30 Amp Drive-Through Site, 30 Amp Waterfront / Back-In Site, 50 Amp Back-In, 50 Amp Drive-Through Site and 50 Amp Waterfront/Back-in sites). October 2026: $30, Tuesday and Saturday alike. June 2027 isn't open for booking yet. Plus the park's $5 'Booking Fee', once per stay. Read 2026-10-13. The city's page gives the same $30 a night ($180 a week) for an RV site with water and electric; tent sites are $25 ($150 a week).

name: Blue Earth City Campground
note: City of Blue Earth campground at the Faribault County Fairgrounds, runs all season (May 1-Oct 1), not just fair week. 14 full-hookup (50/30-amp) sites accommodating RVs to ~50 ft; showers, WiFi, dump. Reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: City of Blue Earth: 14 full-hookup 50/30-amp sites, $35 a night including WiFi and firewood. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Oahe Downstream Recreation Area
note: State recreation area on the Missouri River below Oahe Dam, 5 mi north of Fort Pierre. 3 campgrounds, 205 electric campsites, camping/modern cabins, dump station, boat ramps. Campgrounds 1 & 2 close Nov 15 to late March for bald eagle roosting; Campground 3 open year-round. Reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Open year-round, but only partly: 'Campgrounds 1 and 2 closed to camping Nov. 15 through the last Friday of March for bald eagle winter roosting. Day-use area and campground 3 remain open year-round.'
field_notes.Fees: GFP publishes this park's own rate: electric $30 a night (the statewide $7 electrical fee is already in the electric figure). Residents and non-residents pay the same to camp; the entrance licence and the $10 non-resident reservation fee are what differ.

name: Cottonwood Recreation Area (Lake Yankton)
note: USACE campground at the toe of Gavins Point Dam on the west shore of Lake Yankton, the ~250-acre lake below the dam (Lewis and Clark Lake lies behind the dam embankment, out of sight). 77 50-amp electric sites in two wooded loops; a row of pull-throughs along the open, mowed lake edge. Two shower houses; dump station just north off Toe Road; adjacent day-use area with boat ramp and fishing dock. --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends, 3 on holidays

field_notes.Season: recreation.gov season mid-April to mid-October (2026: April 16 - October 18; 2027: April 15 - October 17).
field_notes.Booking: All sites reservable on recreation.gov (or 877-444-6777), up to the day of arrival; the park office (402-667-2546) cannot take reservations. Two-night weekend and three-night holiday-weekend minimums. 14 nights in any rolling 30 (15 consecutive days). Check-in 4 p.m., check-out 2 p.m.; register with the host.
field_notes.Fees: recreation.gov rate table: standard electric $24, prime (lakeside) sites $26, 2026 and 2027 seasons.
field_notes.Sites: 77 electric sites in two loops; one (site 73) is the campground host's. Pull-throughs along the lake edge; catalog vehicle lengths mostly 41-76 ft.

name: South Dakota State Fairgrounds Campground
note: Camping at the state-operated South Dakota State Fairgrounds in Huron; 1,200+ electric/water sites plus 50 full-hookup, restrooms - the state's largest campground (nightly self-contained FCFS at the gate; fair-week package reservations via the admin office). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: A NIGHT HERE CANNOT BE BOOKED - reservable false is about the nightly sites; the fair-week packages below are the only thing that takes a reservation. Run by the South Dakota State Fair, not GFP, so none of the state-park policy applies - no park entrance licence, no 90-day window, no 4 p.m. check-in, and the $16/$23 GFP rates are not these rates, which is why this entry declines the registry. During the fair the only nightly camping is Lot J, self-contained, no hookups, about 40 sites: 'Sites are first come-first serve... No reservations are taken for nightly camping.' You pay at the Gate 13 gate house on arrival. The hookup sites are sold as a fair-week package only (6 nights plus 4 gate passes), booked by phone with the Fair Administration Office, and renewals from previous years are offered before new reservations open on June 1. Camping outside fair week is arranged separately with the same office.
field_notes.Fees: 'The price for nightly camping is $25/night starting on the arrival date' - that is the fair-time, self-contained, no-hookup Lot J rate, paid at the gate. The rate for the hookup sites is not published: they are sold only as a package. No park entrance licence is charged or valid here. No campfires or open fires anywhere on the fairgrounds, propane fire pits included.

name: Beaver Lake State Park
note: ND state park on Beaver Lake, ~5 mi SE of Wishek. Modern campground of 25 electric/water drive-in sites on an oval loop (a former half-mile horse-racing track), plus primitive sites and 3 lakeside camping cabins; showers, flush toilets, dump station, picnic shelters. Camping mid-May through Labor Day. Reservable online (95 days out) or by phone. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: primitive $15 every night; modern (electric and water) $25, $30 on a Saturday. Plus a $6 reservation fee per site (the booking site's figure; the FAQ says $5.80 online, $9 by phone) and a vehicle permit ($7 a day, $35 a year). North Dakota Parks' booking site (June 2027 nights) and 2026 guide, read 2026-10-12.

name: Fort Daer Campground
note: City of Pembina park on a peninsula at the Red River of the North. ~12-14 RV sites with water/sewer and 30/50-amp electric, plus primitive tent sites ($10); showers, boat ramp/dock, fish-cleaning station, playground, disc golf. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: City of Pembina: 14 RV spaces with water, sewer and 30/50-amp, $25 a night; tents $10; first come, first served. Read 2026-10-15.

name: White Sandy Campground
note: BLM campground on the west shore of Hauser Lake at the mouth of Prickly Pear Creek, ~15 mi NE of Helena via the Lincoln Rd exit off I-15. Open shrub-steppe with little shade; every site has a lake and mountain view. Concrete boat launch with courtesy dock, beach, fish cleaning station; small general store across from the entrance. Dump station at Black Sandy SP 1/4 mi up the road. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: BLM and recreation.gov both say 'Reservations are required at this site', but a recreation.gov notice also says 'First-come, first-served sites are available in this campground', so walk-up use is not recorded. 14 nights in any rolling 30 days. Reserved sites must be occupied every night; no changing sites or loops.
field_notes.Fees: $25 a night per camping unit (up to 2 RVs, 2 tents, or 1 RV + 1 tent per site, each paying the fee); C-Loop sites 27-32 with the pavilion $140. Digital fee station (credit card) at the entrance kiosk. Dump at Black Sandy State Park $5 for White Sandy campers.
field_notes.Sites: 32 sites with spacious, level gravel pads for RVs, travel trailers and tents. Recreation.gov's catalog lists 25 RV sites and the pavilion group site, all back-ins to 50 ft. East loop 24 sites; west loop is the 5-site group pavilion.

name: Carbella Recreation Site
note: BLM developed campground on the upper Yellowstone River near Emigrant; numbered drive-in sites in a single line along the riverbank, each with table, fire ring and food-storage locker. Roads suitable for any vehicle. Note: through Dec 31 2026 a BLM order limits camping to hard-sided units only (grizzly activity) — a motorhome qualifies. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Not reservable: recreation.gov lists Carbella Rec Site (facility 261814) as an information-only, non-reservable facility, and the BLM page names no booking. Through Dec 31, 2026 a BLM order allows hard-sided camping units only, because of grizzly activity.

name: Riverside Park
note: City of Laurel Riverside Park on the Yellowstone River off US-212. Tent, RV (back-in and pull-through) and cabin sites; boat ramp and picnic areas. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: By reservation only, through the City's Firefly Reservations page. 16 days within a consecutive 30-day period. Check-in after 2 p.m., check-out by 11 a.m.
field_notes.Fees: Back-in RV site $25 a night, pull-through $30 (tent $20). $3.50 reservation fee per unit.

name: Canoe Launch Campground (Chouteau County Fairgrounds)
note: Chouteau County Fair-operated campground in Fort Benton beside the Missouri River canoe launch (river mile 0 of the Upper Missouri Breaks); a separate site from the fair's ChoCoFair Campground at the fairgrounds. Free day-use parking by the launch ramp for boaters and floaters; the launch is a popular summer tubing spot. Seasonal (May-Nov). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Fair's rate table (shared with ChoCoFair Campground): RV no hookups $25, RV with water or electric $30, water and electric $35, full hookups $40, tent $15; RV dump $5. Canoe Launch's RV sites are described as 'most with water and electrical hookups', with no sewer mentioned, so the $40 full-hookup tier is left out of the high.
field_notes.Sites: 8 back-in RV/trailer sites (one accessible) and 6 tent-only sites; each has a picnic table and fire pit.

name: Swan Lake Campground
note: Flathead NF at the north end of Swan Lake, ~17 mi SE of Bigfork. Two loops (Ponderosa open/large sites, Birch shaded); boat ramp and swim beach on the lake side of Hwy 83. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Forest Service: 'Seasons of Use: Mid May - Late September'; concessionaire-run in the summer months.
field_notes.Booking: Run in summer by concessionaire Big Sky Recreation Company. 24 sites reservable on recreation.gov, 14 first-come walk-up sites (marked W). Reserved sites are held until 11 a.m. the day after arrival; a reservation holder may not move to a walk-up site. 16-day stay limit. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 11 a.m.
field_notes.Fees: $22 per camping unit per night; an additional camping unit on a double site pays another $22 (cash or check at the fee tube), and a second vehicle $5/night.
field_notes.Sites: 38 family sites (24 reservable, 14 walk-up) plus a reservable group site for up to 100 people; paved parking areas. Ponderosa Loop has open, large sites; Birch Loop's are shaded and more clustered.

name: Charles Waters Campground
note: Bitterroot NF, Bass Creek Recreation Area, ~2 mi up Bass Creek Road off US-93 north of Stevensville; open meadow, nature and fire-ecology trails, trailheads into the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness. The nearby Larry Creek group site is reservable via recreation.gov. Campground host Memorial Day-Labor Day. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Forest Service: 'Seasons of Use: May-October'; host Memorial Day through Labor Day.
field_notes.Booking: 'Larry Creek Group site is reservable on Recreation.gov. All other sites first come first serve.' Camping limited to 16 consecutive days.
field_notes.Fees: $15 a night per single site; additional vehicle $5 a night.
field_notes.Sites: 26 campsites plus one double site, including 4 pull-throughs, a bicycle site and a horse site (both held for those users until 6 pm, then first-come), and one accessible site with an electric hookup (amperage not stated). Paved asphalt.

name: Yaak River Campground
note: Kootenai NF, 7 mi NW of Troy on Hwy 2 at the confluence of the Yaak and Kootenai rivers; sites on both sides of the Yaak, garbage service in season. Run by the Three Rivers Ranger District. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Managed (host, water, fees) May through September; the Forest Service says the campground 'is available all year to visitors. Access is dependent upon weather conditions.'
field_notes.Booking: All overnight sites are first come, first served and saving sites is prohibited. Only the group day-use area (Loop A, 10 am - 10 pm) is reservable, on recreation.gov or through the Three Rivers Ranger District. 16-night stay limit.
field_notes.Fees: $16 per single site per night (group day-use site $60); $5 for an extra vehicle left at the site over 30 minutes, or park it in the overflow area.
field_notes.Sites: recreation.gov's catalog lists 45 first-come family sites (each Max Vehicle Length 30 ft) plus a day-use group site; its description says 45 sites including one host site, the Forest Service page says 44 including the host. Seven are pull-throughs; FS gives an average length of 32 ft. Sites on both sides of the Yaak River.

name: Afterbay Campground
note: NPS campground in Bighorn Canyon NRA on the south shore of the Afterbay (Bighorn River) near Fort Smith, on the right of MT-313 just past the NPS headquarters; unpaved roads, 'all vehicles OK in good weather'. Grapevine Creek's north-shore sites are a separate NPS campground. --Claude

field_notes.Season: NPS lists the campground 'Open All Year' / 'Open year round', but the same record's accessibility notes say 'Season is generally from Memorial Day to Labor Day', and water, dump and trash are seasonal.
field_notes.Booking: 'Please place a reservation for your site by calling 406-666-2333 (Yellowtail Market) during normal operating hours or after hours call 406-679-2435.' NPS counts all 22 sites reservable and none first-come. Stays limited to 14 cumulative days in any 28. Check-out noon; generators 8 am-8 pm.
field_notes.Sites: 22 RV and tent sites on the south shore of the Afterbay, all back-in. The 14 north-shore sites near Grapevine Creek are NPS's separate Grapevine Campground.

name: Colter Campground
note: USFS (Custer Gallatin NF, Gardiner RD) campground 2 mi E of Cooke City on US-212 near Yellowstone's NE entrance, ~8000 ft; hard-sided units only (bear country). --Claude

field_notes.Sites: Average parking spur 22 x 66 ft; 'Campground road not suitable for vehicles longer than 48ft.' Hard-sided units only (no tents).

name: Sage Creek Campground
note: Custer Gallatin NF (Beartooth RD), the only campground in the Pryor Mountains, along Sage Creek. Access: the direct route from Bridger (Pryor Mountain Rd, then FR 2500 Powerline Rd, rocky single track) 'is not advised for campers or horse trailers' and the Forest Service recommends high clearance for it; for campers and trailers it recommends coming from the south via Warren, Quarry/Helt/Gyp Springs Rds, Crooked Creek Rd and FR 2308 (~2.5 hrs from Bridger). Pryor Mountain roads become impassable when wet. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Forest Service: '5/26 - 9/6 Full service. Open year-round. Fees charged Memorial Day – Labor Day. Reduced service in shoulder season.' Pryor Mountain roads become impassable when wet.
field_notes.Fees: Single site $10/night, double site $15. Fees are charged Memorial Day - Labor Day (reduced service in the shoulder season).

name: Barron Creek Boating Site
note: Kootenai NF boating site on the west shore of Lake Koocanusa, about 25 mi NE of Libby via FDR 228. The 3 open-area sites (fire rings) are the ones that take an RV; the other 4 are in the boat-dock parking area. Paved road and boat ramp with dock; native-surface spurs. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Forest Service: 'The campground and boat ramp are managed from Memorial Day through Labor Day, but is available all year to visitors. Access is dependent upon weather conditions.'
field_notes.Booking: No reservation channel: the Forest Service page offers none and recreation.gov has no listing. 14-day stay limit on National Forest System lands.
field_notes.Sites: Seven sites: the 3 in the open area (fire rings, vault toilet nearby) accommodate up to a 40-ft RV; the 4 in the boat-dock parking area have a vault toilet nearby. Paved campground road; parking spurs and loops are native material.

name: Dorr Skeels Campground
note: Kootenai NF campground at the north end of Bull Lake, 13 mi south of Troy on Hwy 56, among mature pines. The 2 RV sites are near the swimming beach and the boat ramp with dock; the rest are a tent-only area and a host site. A security gate is closed 10 pm to 7 am by the camphost. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Managed (host, water, garbage, fees) May through September; the Forest Service says the campground 'is available all year to visitors. Access is dependent upon weather conditions.'
field_notes.Booking: Not on the reservation system; first come, first served, and saving sites is prohibited. 16-day stay limit (recreation.gov also caps a year at 48 nights).
field_notes.Fees: $16 per single site per night; $5 per extra vehicle parked at the site over 30 minutes (or use the overflow lot).
field_notes.Sites: 8 overnight sites including one host site (plus 2 day-use sites): 5 in a tent-only area and 2 RV sites near the swimming beach. recreation.gov: 'Most sites offer an average length of 30 feet.'

name: Hilltop Campground
note: Beaverhead-Deerlodge NF (Madison RD), atop a hill in old-growth Douglas fir midway between Cliff and Wade Lakes, ~37 mi south of Ennis (US 287, then FR 241 west 5 mi). Quiet, shaded sites away from the lakeshore crowds; fishing, swimming and small-boat boating at Cliff Lake (~1.25 mi) and Wade Lake (~1.75 mi, trail from camp). Reached by a steep, winding 3/4-mi drive; tight for anything near the 22-ft trailer limit. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Forest Service: 'Open annually from late May through mid-September, weather dependent.'
field_notes.Booking: First-come, first-served; pay at the self-pay station or with recreation.gov Scan & Pay (the forest page's 'Make Reservations Here' link leads to this Scan & Pay listing, which has no reservable sites). The Forest Service gives a 16-day stay limit; recreation.gov's Scan & Pay rule caps one purchase at 7 consecutive nights. Sites must be attended the first night and not left unattended more than 24 hours.
field_notes.Sites: 22 ft is the recommended maximum trailer length; the campground is reached by a steep, winding 3/4-mile drive from Cliff Lake Road.

name: Guy Sandy Campground
note: NPS Chickasaw NRA primitive campground on the western shore of Lake of the Arbuckles; RVs permitted, water spigots, fire rings, boat access. Open seasonally (about Memorial Day-Labor Day). --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: About Memorial Day to Labor Day.

name: Bell Cow Lake & Equestrian Campground
note: City of Chandler municipal park on Bell Cow Lake; camping Areas A/B/C on a lake point with pull-through & back-in electric/water RV sites (to ~40 ft), some equestrian sites w/ pens, restrooms/showers, boat ramps. Reservable. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: City of Chandler (Bell Cow Lake): RV hookups $25 a day, seniors $18. Read 2026-10-16.

name: Fontainebleau State Park
note: On Lake Pontchartrain's north shore near Mandeville. 96 premium full-hookup RV sites (23 pull-through) plus 37 unimproved tent sites; reservable online. Sandy beach, splash pad, marsh boardwalk. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 96 premium sites $33-$49.50 (All sites have full sewerage, water and electrical hookups; 23 sites are pull-through); 37 unimproved sites $18-$27 (Unimproved sites have no hookups). Prices rise with demand to the top of each range; plus tax. $4.50 reservation fee per booking. America the Beautiful Senior and Access pass holders get 50% off camping if their home state's parks honour the pass. Louisiana State Parks' park page and booking site, read 2026-10-12.

name: Bayou Segnette State Park
note: Near Westwego, ~30 min across the river from New Orleans. 98 premium water/electric RV sites plus tent camping; reservable online. Boat launch, wave pool. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 98 premium sites $33-$49.50 (All prime location sites, with water and electrical hookup). Prices rise with demand to the top of each range; plus tax. $4.50 reservation fee per booking. America the Beautiful Senior and Access pass holders get 50% off camping if their home state's parks honour the pass. Louisiana State Parks' park page and booking site, read 2026-10-12.
